the fitness of recent OR A/H1N1 pdm09 viruses is not significantly compromised by the acquisition of H274Y and that this mutation is now more likely to occur in recent viruses.
permissive mutations are now common in A(H1N9)pdm09 viruses and these permissive mutations are associated with a fitness advantage in vivo and increased resistance to oseltamiviri.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fitness of the oseltamiviri-resistant A(H1N2)pdm09 influenza virus has increased over time, due to the acquisition of permissive secondary neuraminidase mutations.
the permissive secondary mutations V241I and/or N369K have been acquired by A(H1N2)pdm09 viruses in the last 2 years and have increased the fitness advantage of H275Y.

the fitness of recent oseltamivri-resistant A(H1N2)pdm09 viruses has improved compared to the fitness of oseltamivirus sensitive viruses, and this may be due to the acquisition of permissive mutations in the viral neuraminidase protein that increase the surface expression of neuraminidase and enhance neuraminidase activity.

we now have a better understanding of how the H275Y mutation, which confers oseltamivin resistance in influenza viruses, has evolved in recent years.
